title: Kaplansky direct-summand decomposition
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M$ be an $R$-module that is isomorphic to a direct sum $\bigoplus_{j\in J}N_j$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] of $R$-modules, and assume each $N_j$ is countably generated (it has an at most countable subset whose finite $R$-linear combinations exhaust $N_j$). If $P$ is an $R$-module that is a direct summand of $M$, meaning there are $R$-linear maps $a:P\to M$ and $b:M\to P$ with $b\circ a=\mathrm{id}_P$, then $P$ is isomorphic to a direct sum $\bigoplus_{i\in I}Q_i$ of countably generated $R$-modules.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 058X (theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum), line 20471 and proof through line 20570

proof.text: Fix the given direct-sum isomorphism and hence regard $M$ as $\bigoplus_{j\in J}N_j$ with its finite-support coordinates [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. The map $a$ is injective since $ba=1$, so identify the original $P$ with $a(P)\subseteq M$; its inverse on the image is $b$. Put $e=ab$. Then $e^2=a(ba)b=e$, its image is this copy of $P$, and $e(p)=p$ for $p\in P$. Also $m=e(m)+(m-e(m))$ has second term in $\ker b$, so $M=P\oplus\ker b$. For $A\subseteq J$, let $M_A$ consist of families supported in $A$, and let $\pi_A:M\to M_A$ erase coordinates outside $A$. This is linear and fixes $M_A$ by its coordinate formula.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20476–20484 and 20500–20505; fixed-coordinate version of the two decompositions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-countable-coordinate-closure] with $f=e$ and $C=\{j\}$ for each $j\in J$. Choose an at most countable set $D_j\subseteq J$ containing $j$ with $e(M_{D_j})\subseteq M_{D_j}$. These choices are made over the set $J$; no bound on the size of $R$ or of $N_j$ is used. The complementary projection $1-e$ also preserves $M_{D_j}$, since $x-e(x)\in M_{D_j}$ whenever $x\in M_{D_j}$.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20511–20552: countable matrix/support-closure step.

proof.text: Choose a well-order of $J$ and identify it with an ordinal $\kappa$. Define sets $A_\alpha\subseteq J$ for $\alpha\leq\kappa$ by transfinite recursion: $A_0=\varnothing$; $A_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}A_\beta$ at a nonzero limit; if $A_\alpha=J$, put $E_\alpha=\varnothing$, and otherwise put $E_\alpha=D_j$ for the least $j\notin A_\alpha$; set $A_{\alpha+1}=A_\alpha\cup E_\alpha$. Each $E_\alpha$ is at most countable. Let $M_\alpha=M_{A_\alpha}$. Inductively $e(M_\alpha)\subseteq M_\alpha$: at a successor every element of $M_{A_\alpha\cup E_\alpha}$ is a sum of an element supported in $A_\alpha$ and one supported in $E_\alpha$, both preserved by $e$; at a limit any finite support in the increasing union lies in one earlier $A_\beta$, so $M_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}M_\beta$ and is preserved as well. The base is $e(0)=0$.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20500–20530 and 20555–20565: the transfinite recursion and its successor/limit invariants.

proof.text: The recursion exhausts $J$ by stage $\kappa$. More precisely, prove $\{\beta:\beta<\alpha\}\subseteq A_\alpha$ for every $\alpha\leq\kappa$ by ordinal induction. At $0$ this is empty. At a successor all indices below $\alpha$ are already in $A_\alpha$; if $\alpha$ is absent then it is the least omitted index, so $E_\alpha=D_\alpha$ contains it. If it is already present, nothing needs adding to cover the initial segment through $\alpha$. At a nonzero limit $\lambda$, any $\beta<\lambda$ lies in $A_{\beta+1}\subseteq A_\lambda$, since $\beta+1<\lambda$. Thus $A_\kappa=J$ and $M_\kappa=M$. This argument still enumerates indices of zero summands, so no inference that a missing summand must be nonzero is needed.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20555–20560: transfinite induction showing exhaustion.

proof.text: Put $P_\alpha=P\cap M_\alpha$. The equality $P_\alpha=e(M_\alpha)$ follows in both directions: stability places $e(x)$ in $M_\alpha$ and in $P$; conversely $p\in P\cap M_\alpha$ satisfies $p=e(p)$. Hence $P_0=0$, $P_\kappa=P$, and $P_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}P_\beta$ at every nonzero limit, using the union equality for $M_\lambda$. For each $\alpha<\kappa$, the map $r_\alpha:P_{\alpha+1}\to P_\alpha$ given by $p\mapsto e(\pi_{A_\alpha}(p))$ is linear and lands in $e(M_\alpha)=P_\alpha$. It fixes $P_\alpha$, since $\pi_{A_\alpha}(p)=p=e(p)$ there. Thus every successor inclusion of the $P_\alpha$ has an explicit retraction. No commutation of $e$ with the coordinate projection is assumed.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20489–20494: splitting the induced filtration on P; explicit retraction in coordinates.

proof.text: Fix $\alpha<\kappa$ and put $B_\alpha=A_{\alpha+1}\setminus A_\alpha\subseteq E_\alpha$. Choose at most countable generating subsets $G_j\subseteq N_j$ for $j\in B_\alpha$. The union of their canonical images is at most countable and generates $M_{B_\alpha}$, because each coordinate family has finite support [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. The map $M_{B_\alpha}\to P_{\alpha+1}/P_\alpha$ sending $z$ to $e(z)+P_\alpha$ is linear with the quotient operations of [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. It is surjective: for $p\in P_{\alpha+1}$ decompose its coordinates as $p=y+z$ with $y\in M_\alpha$ and $z\in M_{B_\alpha}$; then $p=e(p)=e(y)+e(z)$ and $e(y)\in P_\alpha$, so its class is the class of $e(z)$. The images of the displayed countable generators therefore generate $P_{\alpha+1}/P_\alpha$. If $B_\alpha$ is empty this quotient is zero and has the empty generating set.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20494–20499 and 20530–20533: countable generation of successive quotients, via an explicit surjection instead of the displayed quotient direct-sum identification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-split-transfinite-module-filtration] to $X=P$ and the ordinal-indexed family $(P_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\kappa}$: steps 4–5 give its endpoints, continuity, and split successor inclusions. It yields $P\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha<\kappa}(P_{\alpha+1}/P_\alpha)$. Set $I=\{\alpha:\alpha<\kappa\}$ and $Q_\alpha=P_{\alpha+1}/P_\alpha$; step 6 proves that every $Q_\alpha$ is countably generated. Transport this isomorphism back to the original module $P$ using the inverse $b:a(P)\to P$ from step 1. When $J$ is empty, $\kappa=0$, the retract $P$ is zero, and this is the empty direct sum.
